findings.statement: A two-edge peak-response approximation improves aggregate physical voltage error, but the original gain is concentrated in one contact condition.

reliability.rationale: The retained evidence supports the stated narrow conclusion under Whole pulse widths across six sensor/contact conditions; ten pulses within a file are repeated apparatus observations. Strong adverse evidence: Only contact 110 kHz improves against constant gain; five other conditions worsen. Six files at one width are not six independent sensor-transfer experiments.

mechanism.rationale: Causal edge superposition is useful as an ansatz. Direct resonance/timebase interpretation is contradicted by separately measured waveforms.

novelty.rationale: Damped oscillators and constant-Q constraints are established; no new resonance physics is certified. This review uses retained prior-art records only; it performs no new literature priority adjudication.

significance.rationale: The measured endpoint and matched controls supply a useful reproducible local benchmark. Whole pulse widths across six sensor/contact conditions; ten pulses within a file are repeated apparatus observations.

reproducibility.rationale: Frozen equations/model states and numerical evidence are present and hash-bound here. This scientific document review is separate from independent computational replay; execution validity must be supplied by that review and the raw-preparation audit.

impact.rationale: Potential monitoring, calibration or experiment-planning value is bounded by the stated endpoint. No operational intervention, measured deployment savings, clinical effect or independent real-world benefit is demonstrated in this portfolio.
